question: According to recent Commission communications, as part of the EU’s anti-racism strategy 2026-2030, initiatives to combat specific forms of ‘hate’ are being explored, including through coordination with civil society organisations and platforms.

Concern has arisen that, through broad or vague definitions of ‘hate speech’, those initiatives could affect the legitimate exercise of freedom of expression and end up driving an ideological interpretation which, under the pretext of tackling racism, promotes Islam as a political and cultural phenomenon and fosters migration policies that are not subject to proper democratic debate.

In this context, it is essential to distinguish between the protection of religious freedom and the legitimate right to express criticism of radical Islamism as a political ideology, a phenomenon that has been the focus of attention in a number of Member States. It is also necessary to check how much public funding has already been allocated to initiatives and programmes in these areas. In the light of the above: 1.

What EU financial resources, broken down by heading and beneficiary – and including disaggregated data, amounts, budget lines, beneficiaries and allocation criteria for these funds, have been allocated over the past five years to programmes, projects or initiatives connected with the promotion of Islam, efforts to tackle ‘Islamophobia’, and integration policies?
How will the Commission ensure that due regard is given to the principle of subsidiarity and to Member State competences in the areas of civil liberties, security and integration?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.7.2026) In line with Article 17 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), the Commission engages in a dialogue with religious and non-confessional organisations. However, it does not finance any project aiming at promoting Islam or any other religion.

The Anti-Racism Strategy 2026-2030 refers to the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values programme (CERV)1, adopted in 2021 as one of the main instruments for supporting antiracism and anti-discrimination initiatives. Under its equality, rights, and gender equality strand, the programme focuses on combating inequalities and discrimination based inter alia on race, religion or belief, including anti-Muslim hatred.

EU funding is awarded based on clear eligibility, exclusion, selection and award criteria. The Commission carries out rigorous selection processes. While most projects funded over the past five years address all forms of racism, seven projects address more specifically the fight against anti-Muslim hatred2. Among these, only the project RADAR is still under implementation3.
The Financial Transparency System4 (FTS) provides all requested information on recipients of EU funding and the Funding and Tenders Portal5 provides all requested information on funded projects.

The Commission respects the principle of subsidiarity in all its actions, including when it comes to the Anti-racism Strategy6, which is a Communication to the European Parliament and the Council presenting the strategic objectives of the Commission in combatting racism within the EU.

Similarly, as regards the integration of migrants, the Action Plan on Integration and Inclusion 2021-20277 and the Strategy on Migration and Asylum8 focus on supporting Member States’ actions in this area, in line with the rules of Article 79(4) TFEU.
